items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015

ctx.x: We’ll see. It depends on what you say.

As a bassist in a jazz group, or frankly as a bassist in any group, there is a lot of function in your job description. You have to function rhythmically and you have to function harmonically. And I’ve discovered after all these years and after having listened to hundreds of other bassists, that there are limited numbers of ways of effectively guiding a band through the harmony of the song and the bass lines that we construct in the moment have to function to help shape the harmony. In other words, if we’ve all…

fond of Ron Carter’s bass lines. When Ron Carter walks a bass line I can often hear the implied harmony between the major resting places in a song. It’s like, oh yeah that would be a diminished chord and that would be a dominant chord, and that gets me to the next place. It’s all in there. Paul Chambers also.
